text:
Juuse Saros stopped all 30 shots in Los Angeles, and the Predators won their fifth straight with a 3-0 shutout of the Kings. Saros was a 99th overall pick in 2013 who spent 2014-15 posting a .929 save percentage in Finland's Liiga for HPK, and on this night he looked the part of a goalie carrying a team. By our numbers he saved about 2.9 goals more than the quality of those shots should have allowed.

Filip Forsberg supplied the offense, scoring twice on snap shots, in the first period and again in the second, with Nils Hoglander assisting on both. Adam Wilsby added the third late in the final period on a wrist shot. Forsberg's second goal was a 7% look by our measure, the kind of chance that usually doesn't go in.

The game itself was closer than the score suggests. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, finished level, 2.89 for NSH and 2.88 for LAK. We'd have given LAK a slight edge on a deserved-to-win basis, which is the share of simulated replays of every shot a team wins: 54% for the Kings, 46% for the Predators. Los Angeles attempted 66 shots to Nashville's 51 and dominated the third period, out-chancing the Predators 1.17 to 0.67 in expected goals. Saros answered every time, and Anton Forsberg in the Kings' net gave up the three goals Nashville managed.

The Predators carry a five-game winning streak out of Los Angeles. The Kings were shut out at home and now look for the finishing touch their chances never quite found.
